alt: 空气炸锅豆泥芝士薄饼

summary: Vegetarian. A tortilla folded over tinned beans and grated cheese and crisped in six or seven minutes. A low-cost lunch using cupboard staples and refrigerated cheese.

ingredients.note: Wheat tortillas contain gluten. Corn tortillas crisp beautifully but crack when folded cold, so warm them first.

ingredients.item: Tinned red kidney or black beans, drained and rinsed
ingredients.note: Tinned beans are already cooked. Keep the rest of the tin in a covered container in the fridge and use it within a couple of days.
For a vegetarian kitchen, check the packet says it is made without animal rennet.

ingredients.item: Ground cumin or smoked paprika, salt and pepper

ingredients.note: Brush on the outside to help the tortilla crisp.

method.instruction: Mash the beans roughly with the cumin, salt and pepper, spread them over half of each tortilla, scatter the cheese on top and fold the tortilla over into a half-moon.
Brush the outside of each folded tortilla with a little oil, then push two or three cocktail sticks through the open edge to pin it shut. An unpinned tortilla is light enough for the fan to lift.
Set the air fryer to 180°C, preheating only if your appliance manual calls for it, and lay the quesadillas flat in a single layer without overlapping them.

Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, turning once at about 4 minutes, until the outside is blistered and crisp and the cheese has melted. The tinned beans are already cooked and the cheese is ready to eat; heat the filling through while browning the tortilla.

Count and remove all cocktail sticks before eating. After cooking, switch off, unplug and let the appliance cool before cleaning. Follow its manual for removable parts, soaking and cleaning products; never immerse the electrical unit or assume water alone is enough.

yield_note: Two quesadillas — lunch for two, or one large plate for one. About 12 minutes in total. Editorial measuring convention for these original notes: tablespoon 20 mL; teaspoon 5 mL. These are volume measures, not gram conversions.

caveats: A loose tortilla is light enough for the fan to lift it against the element on some models. Fold it, pin it shut, keep it flat, and do not leave the machine running unattended the first time you make it.
Cocktail sticks are easy to forget and easy to bite down on. Count them in and count them out.
Allergens: wheat in flour tortillas, dairy in the cheese. Both are printed on the packets.
Nothing here needs cooking to a temperature: the beans were cooked in the tin and the cheese only has to melt. Drain and rinse the beans, and refrigerate what is left of the tin.
These are practical notes, not kitchen-tested here and never given a professional food-safety review.
